supermarket.note: Either garlic chives or scallions will work, so buy whichever is easier to find.

general.item: sambal oelek or other chili paste

tools.name: Bowl
tools.note: Use a small bowl for mixing the sauce.

tools.name: Pot
tools.note: Use a medium pot for boiling water to loosen the noodles.

tools.name: Heatproof bowl
tools.note: Use a large one, since it is for soaking the noodles.

tools.name: Wok
tools.note: A 12-inch skillet can be used in its place.

tools.name: Wok spatula
tools.note: A wide metal spatula can be used instead.

tools.name: Serving plates
tools.note: Any two plates will do in place of serving plates.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients and divide into two batches
points: Slice the Chinese sausages thinly on a diagonal.
Mince the garlic.
Cut the chives or scallions into 2-inch lengths.
Rinse the bean sprouts and let them drain.
In the small bowl, stir together the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and sambal oelek until the sugar dissolves.
Divide the shrimp, sausage, garlic, bean sprouts, chives, and sauce into two equal portions, one for each batch.

steps.title: Soften the noodles
points: Bring the medium pot of water to a boil.
Put the noodles in the heatproof bowl and pour the boiling water over them.
Gently separate the strands with chopsticks for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until they come apart.
Drain in the colander, toss with 1 teaspoon of oil, and divide into two portions.

steps.title: Stir-fry garlic, sausage and shrimp
points: Heat the wok over high heat until it just begins to smoke, about 2 minutes.
Add 1 1/2 tablespoons of oil, then one portion of garlic and sausage.
Stir for 30 seconds.
Add one portion of shrimp and cook, tossing, for 1 to 2 minutes until pink.

steps.title: Add sauce and toss noodles
points: Add one portion of noodles and pour one portion of sauce over them.
Toss gently with the spatula, lifting from underneath, for 1 to 2 minutes, until the noodles are evenly brown and a few edges have charred.

steps.title: Scramble the egg
points: Push everything to one side of the wok.
Crack 1 egg into the empty space and let it set for 20 seconds, then break it up and fold it through the noodles.

steps.title: Wilt the sprouts and chives
points: Add one portion of bean sprouts and chives and toss for 30 seconds, until the chives wilt.
Turn out onto a plate.
Wipe the wok clean with a paper towel and repeat steps 3 to 6 with the remaining ingredients.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles break into short pieces
troubleshooting.solution: They were stirred too hard or were still cold and stiff. Loosen them fully in hot water first, and lift and fold them with the spatula rather than stirring.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles come out pale and wet instead of smoky
troubleshooting.solution: The wok was crowded or not hot enough. Cook one portion at a time and wait until the wok smokes before adding oil.
They cooked too long. Take them only to pink in step 3, since they keep cooking while the noodles fry.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles stick to the wok
troubleshooting.solution: There was too little oil or the wok was not hot enough when they went in. Make sure the oil shimmers and coats the pan before the noodles go in.
